blocks.en: Chapala Theological Seminary, a ministry of Common Ground Fellowship | Professor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers

blocks.en: This course is drawn from the worship curriculum of Dr. Wayne Cook, who served eleven years as Professor of Pastoral Ministries and Preaching, together with the teaching of Andi Cook, who taught alongside him at the seminary. It reflects not only academic study but decades of pastoral and seminary experience.
blocks.es_reference: Este curso proviene del currículo de adoración del Dr. Wayne Cook, quien sirvió once años como Profesor de Ministerios Pastorales y Predicación, junto con la enseñanza de Andi Cook, quien enseñó a su lado en el seminario. Refleja no solo el estudio académico sino décadas de experiencia pastoral y de seminario.

blocks.en: I. Spirit and Truth: The Verse That Holds It All
blocks.es_reference: I. Espíritu y verdad: el versículo que lo sostiene todo

blocks.en: We have come to the end of the course, and everything we have studied gathers into a single verse: "God is a Spirit, and they that worship Him must worship Him in spirit and in truth" (John 4:24). This is the thread that runs through all eleven units. To worship in spirit and in truth is to worship with both heart and mind, both affection and doctrine. Spirit without truth drifts into sincere error; truth without spirit dries into a cold lecture. We humans are not one-dimensional. We give God our minds AND our praise. The whole of who we are responds to the whole of who God is. That is the heart of worship, and it is where every controversy in worship is finally resolved, by refusing to split what God has joined.
blocks.es_reference: Hemos llegado al final del curso, y todo lo que hemos estudiado se reúne en un solo versículo: "Dios es Espíritu; y los que le adoran, en espíritu y en verdad es necesario que adoren" (Juan 4:24). Este es el hilo que corre por las once unidades. Adorar en espíritu y en verdad es adorar con el corazón y la mente, con afecto y doctrina. El espíritu sin la verdad se desvía en error sincero; la verdad sin el espíritu se seca en una conferencia fría. Los seres humanos no somos unidimensionales. Damos a Dios nuestra mente Y nuestra alabanza. Todo lo que somos responde a todo lo que Dios es. Ese es el corazón de la adoración, y es donde toda controversia en la adoración finalmente se resuelve, al rehusar separar lo que Dios ha unido.

blocks.en: II. Gathering the Traditions
blocks.es_reference: II. Reuniendo las tradiciones

blocks.en: In Unit 10 we saw that each great tradition cultivates a true feeling that worship should include. Catholic worship cultivates awe; Orthodox worship cultivates mystery; Coptic worship cultivates endurance; the Reformed cultivate the mind; the charismatic and Pentecostal cultivate joy; the Black church cultivates participation; evangelicals cultivate focus on the preached Word. Every one of these is biblical somewhere in the Scriptures.
blocks.es_reference: En la Unidad 10 vimos que cada gran tradición cultiva un sentimiento verdadero que la adoración debe incluir. La adoración católica cultiva el asombro; la adoración ortodoxa cultiva el misterio; la adoración copta cultiva la perseverancia; los reformados cultivan la mente; los carismáticos y pentecostales cultivan el gozo; la iglesia negra cultiva la participación; los evangélicos cultivan el enfoque en la Palabra predicada. Cada uno de estos es bíblico en alguna parte de las Escrituras.

blocks.en: And we saw the danger: to mistake the part we know for the whole. Awe without joy makes God distant; joy without awe makes Him casual; mystery without truth becomes superstition; endurance without grace becomes legalism; the Word without affection becomes mere lecture. Each tradition is tempted to take its own true feeling and treat it as the whole of worship. The mature pastor refuses that error. He learns from Isaiah and David, from Calvin and the Coptic liturgies, from the spirituals sung in chains, and he hears through them all one voice, the worshipping church. He honors what Scripture honors in each, with humility.
blocks.es_reference: Y vimos el peligro: confundir la parte que conocemos con el todo. El asombro sin gozo hace a Dios distante; el gozo sin asombro lo hace casual; el misterio sin verdad se vuelve superstición; la perseverancia sin gracia se vuelve legalismo; la Palabra sin afecto se vuelve mera conferencia. Cada tradición es tentada a tomar su propio sentimiento verdadero y tratarlo como el todo de la adoración. El pastor maduro rehúsa ese error. Aprende de Isaías y David, de Calvino y las liturgias coptas, de los espirituales cantados en cadenas, y oye a través de todos ellos una voz, la iglesia adoradora. Honra lo que la Escritura honra en cada uno, con humildad.

blocks.en: III. The Threads Drawn Together
blocks.es_reference: III. Los hilos reunidos

blocks.en: Several threads have run through this whole course, and now we tie them. The room preaches: architecture is theology made visible, and the placement of pulpit, table, and baptistry teaches Word and sacrament without a word. The moods and the prayer elements run parallel: the five moods shape the whole service and the six elements shape a single prayer, both moving God-ward through adoration, thanksgiving, confession, and dedication, so that the service is a large prayer and a prayer is a small service. Worship holds together the pairs we are always tempted to split: Word and sacrament, reverence and joy, the individual and the congregation, tradition and freshness. To worship well is to keep these joined.
blocks.es_reference: Varios hilos han corrido por todo este curso, y ahora los atamos. La sala predica: la arquitectura es teología hecha visible, y la colocación del púlpito, la mesa, y el baptisterio enseña la Palabra y el sacramento sin una palabra. Los ánimos y los elementos de la oración corren paralelos: los cinco ánimos moldean todo el servicio y los seis elementos moldean una sola oración, ambos moviéndose hacia Dios por medio de adoración, acción de gracias, confesión, y dedicación, de modo que el servicio es una oración grande y una oración es un servicio pequeño. La adoración sostiene juntos los pares que siempre somos tentados a separar: Palabra y sacramento, reverencia y gozo, el individuo y la congregación, tradición y frescura. Adorar bien es mantener estos unidos.

blocks.en: What, then, is worship? In a word, worship is the response of the whole person to the God who has revealed Himself. God takes the initiative, He reveals Himself, and we respond, in spirit and in truth, with mind and heart together. And why does it matter? Because God commands it, because He is worthy of it, and because He made us for it. The soul was made for worship and is restless until it worships its Maker.
blocks.es_reference: ¿Qué es, entonces, la adoración? En una palabra, la adoración es la respuesta de toda la persona al Dios que se ha revelado. Dios toma la iniciativa, se revela, y nosotros respondemos, en espíritu y en verdad, con mente y corazón juntos. ¿Y por qué importa? Porque Dios la manda, porque es digno de ella, y porque nos hizo para ella. El alma fue hecha para la adoración y está inquieta hasta que adora a su Hacedor.

blocks.en: IV. The Charge
blocks.es_reference: IV. El encargo

blocks.en: So we close where a course on worship must close, not with information, but with a charge. You have studied the definitions, the history, the planning, the music, the spoken elements, the preaching and the invitation, the ordinances, and the room itself. But all of it is meant to be carried into the leading of a congregation. The pastor is both a worshipper and a teacher of worship. He must first give God his own mind and his own praise, and then he must lead his people into true worship in spirit and in truth.
blocks.es_reference: Así que cerramos donde un curso sobre la adoración debe cerrar, no con información, sino con un encargo. Usted ha estudiado las definiciones, la historia, la planeación, la música, los elementos hablados, la predicación y la invitación, las ordenanzas, y la sala misma. Pero todo ello está destinado a ser llevado al dirigir una congregación. El pastor es tanto un adorador como un maestro de la adoración. Debe primero dar a Dios su propia mente y su propia alabanza, y luego debe dirigir a su pueblo a la verdadera adoración en espíritu y en verdad.

blocks.en: Take everything this course has taught and carry it home to your people. Build a room that says what you mean. Plan a service that moves through the moods toward its climax. Guard the spoken elements. Sing with both depth and joy. Make the gospel visible in the ordinances. And above all, worship God yourself, with your whole heart and your whole mind, so that your people learn what worship is by watching you do it. Go and worship Him. And teach your people to do the same.
blocks.es_reference: Tome todo lo que este curso ha enseñado y llévelo a casa a su pueblo. Construya una sala que diga lo que usted quiere. Planee un servicio que se mueva a través de los ánimos hacia su clímax. Guarde los elementos hablados. Cante con profundidad y gozo. Haga visible el evangelio en las ordenanzas. Y sobre todo, adore usted mismo a Dios, con todo su corazón y toda su mente, para que su pueblo aprenda lo que es la adoración viéndolo a usted hacerlo. Ve y adórale. Y enseña a tu pueblo a hacer lo mismo.

fill.prompt: "God is a Spirit, and they that worship Him must worship Him in spirit and in ____" (John 4:24).

sa.prompt: Synthesize the whole course: how does John 4:24, worship in spirit and in truth, hold everything together?
sa.model: John 4:24, 'God is a Spirit, and they that worship Him must worship Him in spirit and in truth,' holds the whole course together because every element studied — definitions, history, planning, music, spoken elements, ordinances, and the room itself — exists to serve this one balance: worship with both heart and mind, both affection and doctrine. Spirit without truth drifts into sincere error; truth without spirit dries into a cold lecture; the whole course has been teaching how to hold both together.

sa.prompt: Summarize how each major tradition cultivates a true feeling that worship should include.
sa.model: Catholic worship cultivates awe through grand architecture; Orthodox worship cultivates mystery through the iconostasis and chanted liturgy; Coptic worship cultivates endurance through ancient liturgies and extensive fasting; the Reformed cultivate the mind through careful, reasoned preaching; the charismatic and Pentecostal cultivate joy through raised hands and spontaneous praise; the Black church cultivates participation through call-and-response; and evangelicals cultivate focus on the preached Word. Every one of these feelings is biblical somewhere in Scripture.

sa.prompt: Explain the danger in every tradition of mistaking the part we know for the whole of worship.
sa.model: The danger in every tradition is mistaking the part it knows well for the whole of worship: awe without joy makes God distant, joy without awe makes Him casual, mystery without truth becomes superstition, endurance without grace becomes legalism, and the Word without affection becomes mere lecture. Each tradition is tempted to treat its own true feeling as if it were the entirety of what worship should be, rather than one true part of a larger whole.

sa.prompt: How should the mature pastor learn from traditions other than his own?
sa.model: The mature pastor learns from Isaiah and David, from Calvin and the Coptic liturgies, from the spirituals sung in chains, hearing through them all one voice, the worshipping church. He honors what Scripture honors in each tradition, with humility, refusing to dismiss traditions unlike his own simply because they are unfamiliar, and instead seeking the biblical truth each one has genuinely preserved.

sa.prompt: Draw together the thread of 'the room preaches' from across the course.
sa.model: The room preaches thread runs through the course from Unit 4's Reformation furniture, through Unit 9's baptistry and communion table placement, to Unit 10's full development: architecture is theology made visible. The placement of pulpit, table, and baptistry teaches Word and sacrament without a word being spoken, so that every sanctuary confesses a theology through its very layout before the preacher ever opens his mouth.

sa.prompt: Draw together the parallel of the moods and the prayer elements as a thread of the course.
sa.model: The five moods that shape the whole service (recognition, praise, confession, illumination, dedication) run parallel to the six elements that shape a single prayer (adoration, thanksgiving, intercession, petition, confession, dedication), both moving God-ward through the same basic pattern. This means the service is a large prayer and a prayer is a small service — worship has one shape at every scale, whether an hour-long gathering or a two-minute personal prayer.

sa.prompt: What does it mean to give God both our minds and our praise, and why does worship require both?
sa.model: To give God both our minds and our praise means engaging sound doctrine and genuine affection together rather than choosing one over the other. Worship requires both because we are not one-dimensional beings — God made us with minds and emotions together, and a worship that engages only the mind eventually dries up while a worship that engages only the emotions eventually drifts, so the whole person must respond to the whole of who God is.

sa.prompt: Summarize the pairs the capstone holds together: Word and sacrament, reverence and joy, individual and congregation.
sa.model: The capstone holds together Word and sacrament, so that preaching and the ordinances both have their proper place without one crowding out the other; reverence and joy, so that awe before God's holiness does not exclude gladness in His presence; and the individual and the congregation, so that personal devotion and corporate worship both matter and neither replaces the other. Worship holds these pairs together rather than splitting them into opposing camps.

sa.prompt: As a capstone, state in your own words what worship is and why it matters, drawing on the whole course.
sa.model: Worship, in a word, is the response of the whole person to the God who has revealed Himself — God takes the initiative, revealing Himself, and we respond in spirit and in truth, with mind and heart together. It matters because God commands it, because He is worthy of it, and because He made us for it; the soul was made for worship and is restless until it worships its Maker.

sa.prompt: The course closes, 'Go and worship Him. And teach your people to do the same.' What is the charge to the pastor in this closing?
sa.model: The charge to the pastor is that all the course has taught is meant to be carried into the leading of a congregation — he must first give God his own mind and his own praise, then lead his people into true worship in spirit and truth. He is charged to build a room that says what he means, plan services that move toward their climax, guard the spoken elements, sing with depth and joy, make the gospel visible in the ordinances, and above all worship God himself so his people learn worship by watching him do it.
